agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: Stalks just pushed into growing under clear sky. Water is the constraint that ends farms — three points a day still drip even with the ditch, and I will not let a thickening row go thirsty on my watch.
today.expect: East field moisture held high so growing can push toward ripe without a dry spell.

yesterday.why: The new sprout is in and clear sky still pulls three points a day even with the ditch. Water is the constraint that ends farms — better spend eight on wet ground than watch a fresh row dry out.
yesterday.expect: East field moisture back up so the sprout holds through another clear stretch.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: Corn is thickening on its own now. Unused timber is a delay too — a woodpile before we need fence or fuel beats empty hands when the next idea needs boards.
today.expect: Wood stock up while the crop cooks, without burning another morning on the same cistern loop.

yesterday.why: We just spent nothing on the cistern while the harvest and reseeding happened. Heat does not wait, and a cistern that sits still while the next soak is coming is a delay dressed as caution.
yesterday.expect: Cistern topped so tomorrow's watering does not borrow from a thin reserve.
